37 A battery of negligible internal resistance is connected to three resistors, as shown.
2 V
0.4 A
0.3 A
2 V
2 V
The potential difference across each resistor is 2 V.
The current from the battery is 0.4 A and the current through one of the resistors connected in
parallel is 0.3 A.
What is the current through the other resistor connected in parallel and what is the electromotive
force (e.m.f.) of the battery?
current / A
e.m.f. / V
A
0.1
4
B
0.3
4
C
0.1
6
D
0.3
6

hints: Notice the left junction where the $0.4\text{ A}$ from the battery meets the $0.3\text{ A}$ in the upper parallel resistor.
Apply charge conservation at that junction: the $0.4\text{ A}$ entering must equal the sum of the two parallel branch currents leaving.

Trace one complete loop from the battery through the series resistor and then through the parallel pair, adding the $2\text{ V}$ across the series resistor to the $2\text{ V}$ across the parallel combination.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: two $2\text{ V}$ resistors in parallel are in series with one $2\text{ V}$ resistor, with negligible internal resistance.
Use Kirchhoff's first law at the left dot. Current $0.4\text{ A}$ flows toward the dot and $0.3\text{ A}$ flows away through the top branch.
Let the lower branch current be $I$. Then $0.4 = 0.3 + I$, so $I = 0.4 - 0.3 = 0.1\text{ A}$.
Find the e.m.f. using the loop rule. Going round the circuit you cross the series resistor ($2\text{ V}$) and then one parallel branch ($2\text{ V}$).
With $V_{lost}=0$ because internal resistance is negligible, $E = 2\text{ V} + 2\text{ V} = 4\text{ V}$.
Current $0.1\text{ A}$ with e.m.f. $4\text{ V}$ matches the first row of the table. This is option A.

A.explanation: The parallel branch currents sum to $0.4\text{ A}$, so the other current is $0.1\text{ A}$, and the loop p.d. is $2\text{ V}+2\text{ V}=4\text{ V}$ which equals the e.m.f.

B.explanation: Both parallel resistors cannot each carry $0.3\text{ A}$ because their sum $0.6\text{ A}$ would exceed the $0.4\text{ A}$ supplied to the junction.

C.explanation: The $0.1\text{ A}$ branch current is correct, but $6\text{ V}$ adds three $2\text{ V}$ drops instead of one series $2\text{ V}$ plus one parallel $2\text{ V}$.

D.explanation: The $0.3\text{ A}$ value ignores Kirchhoff's first law at the junction and $6\text{ V}$ incorrectly sums all three $2\text{ V}$ resistor voltages in one loop.
